Compare a fetched data frame with the one a capsule was pinned against

Source: R/drift.R
cpsdrft.Rd

Checks whether the data in a freshly downloaded table still look like the data an analysis was built on, column by column. A digest only says whether the bytes changed; this says whether the distributions changed, which is what invalidates a result. Use it when re-running an analysis on a re-released extract.

Usage

cpsdrft(
  ref,
  cur,
  alpha = 0.01,
  psithr = 0.25,
  psiminn = 1000L,
  bins = 10L,
  idelvls = 100L,
  seed = 1L
)

Arguments

ref

Data frame the capsule was built from.

cur

Data frame just fetched.

alpha

Significance level for the drifted flag (default 0.01; deliberately stricter than 0.05 because a wide table runs many tests).

psithr

PSI above which a numeric column is flagged even when its p-value is not significant (default 0.25, the conventional “material shift” line).

psiminn

Minimum size BOTH samples must reach before psithr is allowed to flag a column on its own (default 1000). The PSI bands are large-sample heuristics with no calibrated null distribution: on a few hundred rows, binning noise alone routinely pushes the index past 0.25, so applying the threshold there manufactures drift. Below this size the flag rests on the Kolmogorov-Smirnov p-value, which is calibrated, and the PSI is still reported as an effect size.

bins

Bins passed to drftpsi() (default 10).

idelvls

A character column with more distinct values than this (or at least 20 distinct values covering more than a fifth of the rows) is an identifier, not a distribution: it gets type = "identifier", its unseen_share (the fraction of current rows whose value the reference never had) and drifted = NA. Character columns that parse as dates are compared as dates (type = "date").

seed

Seed for the Monte Carlo branch of the homogeneity test, drfthomog(). The caller's RNG stream is left untouched.

Value

A list of class bricklayer_drift with elements:

columns

a data frame, one row per shared column, with column, type ("numeric", "date", "categorical" or "identifier"), statistic (KS \(D\) or chi-square), p_value, psi, jsdiv, unseen_share (share of current values the reference never had; categorical and identifier columns only), drifted (logical, NA when no test applies) and note (why a column was not tested, or "");

added, removed

character vectors of column names;

nref, ncur

row counts;

alpha, psithr, psiminn

the settings used;

bands

the PSI bands the plots and reports colour by: warn (0.1, or psithr when lower) and fail (psithr);

summ

one binned summary per shared column, for plot(), drfthtml() and drftapp(): missing shares, sizes, summary statistics or the ten largest categories, the PSI bins with each bin's term of the index, a histogram and first-digit counts. Never the rows;

anydrft

logical.

The print method lists the per-column verdicts, drifted columns first.

Details

Runs the appropriate drift test on every shared column and collects the verdicts in one report: drftks() plus drftpsi() for a numeric column, drfthomog() for a categorical one. Columns that appeared or vanished are listed separately, since no test applies to them.

The categorical test is the two-sample homogeneity test, NOT drftchisq() 's goodness-of-fit against a known distribution: the reference here is itself a finite sample, and ignoring its sampling error would report drift too readily.

This is the check that a byte-level digest cannot make. A re-released extract legitimately has a different SHA-256 while being the same data statistically; conversely a column can keep its name, type and row count while having been silently rescaled. cpsdrft() asks whether the DATA moved.

Column types: a column numeric on both sides is "numeric"; a character or factor column whose every value is an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) or date-time on both sides is converted and tested as "date"; a categorical column with more than idelvls distinct values, or with at least 20 distinct values that number more than a fifth of the rows, is an "identifier" and is not tested; anything else is "categorical". Missing values are dropped. For a categorical column the PSI is computed over the reference's categories with every unseen current value pooled into one extra bin.

A column is drifted when its p-value is below alpha, or when its PSI exceeds psithr and both samples have at least psiminn values. anydrft is also TRUE when a column was added or removed. Each column runs one or two tests, so with many columns some will fall below alpha by chance; see scanadj() for a multiplicity correction and drftcal() for an empirical false-alarm rate. A progress bar is shown in an interactive session for many columns.

Errors: either argument not a data frame; alpha not strictly between 0 and 1; psiminn negative; idelvls below 2.

See also

valsch() for the structural check, which this complements rather than replaces.

Examples

set.seed(5)
ref <- data.frame(
  value = stats::rnorm(300),
  size = stats::runif(300, 1, 10),
  grade = sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 300, TRUE)
)

# A fresh draw from the same process: no drift.
same <- data.frame(
  value = stats::rnorm(300),
  size = stats::runif(300, 1, 10),
  grade = sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 300, TRUE)
)
d <- cpsdrft(ref, same)
d$anydrft
#> [1] FALSE

# A silently rescaled column, and a new category, are both caught.
moved <- same
moved$size <- moved$size * 3
moved$grade[1:100] <- "z"
cpsdrft(ref, moved)
#> ── Capsule drift report ──────────────────────────────────────────
#>   ✗ DRIFT DETECTED
#> 
#>   reference rows  300
#>   current rows    300
#>   columns tested  3
#>   alpha           0.01
#> 
#> ── Per-column tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────
#>      column        type  stat      p   psi
#>    ✗   size     numeric 0.743 <2e-16 4.299
#>    ✗  grade categorical   121 <2e-16 4.381
#>    ✓  value     numeric  0.05  0.847 0.092
#> 
#>   plot(x, what = "columns") draws the columns; drfthtml(x, file) writes an interactive report
#> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The PSI is always reported as an effect size, but on a sample this
# small it is not allowed to raise the flag by itself -- binning noise
# alone would clear 0.25. Lower psiminn to override that.
cpsdrft(ref, same)$columns$psi
#> [1] 0.092442043 0.066359848 0.003317333

# Structural changes are reported rather than tested.
cpsdrft(ref, same[, c("value", "grade")])$removed
#> [1] "size"

try(cpsdrft(ref, as.matrix(same)))
#> Error : `ref` and `cur` must both be data frames
